package_info.package_versions: 17.3.1 and below, 17.2.4 and below, 17.1.6 and below
package_info.why_malicious: Multiple critical vulnerabilities allow attackers to perform privilege escalation, server-side request forgery, denial-of-service, and command injection, leading to unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and compromise of critical infrastructure.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker triggers a pipeline as another user due to improper authentication/authorization checks (CVE-2024-6678).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code allows an attacker to trigger a CI/CD pipeline as another user by bypassing proper authentication checks, resulting in privilege escalation and unauthorized code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Triggering actions as another user without their consent is a clear privilege escalation vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only authenticated users should be able to trigger pipelines on their own behalf; this flaw allows impersonation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Impersonation may be used by admins for debugging, but never by unprivileged users.
key_indicators: Pipeline trigger endpoint lacks proper user validation
Ability to specify arbitrary user context

execution_context.file_location: Maven Dependency Proxy URL handler (GitLab EE backend)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker crafts a custom Maven Dependency Proxy URL to perform SSRF (CVE-2024-8635).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes a user-supplied Maven Dependency Proxy URL without proper validation, allowing the attacker to make server-side requests to internal resources, potentially exposing sensitive services.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing user-controlled URLs to be fetched by the server can expose internal-only resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Dependency proxy should only fetch legitimate, external Maven artifacts, not arbitrary URLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching dependencies from public Maven repositories.
key_indicators: Ability to specify internal IPs or hostnames

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a large glm_source parameter to cause DoS (CVE-2024-8124).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fails to properly limit the size of the glm_source parameter, allowing an attacker to send an excessively large value, exhausting server resources and causing denial-of-service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unbounded input can be abused to crash or degrade service availability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: API parameters should be size-limited and validated.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Large parameters may be used for legitimate data transfer, but should be controlled.

execution_context.file_location: Cube server integration logic (GitLab EE backend)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker injects commands into Cube server due to incomplete input filtering (CVE-2024-8640).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code passes user-supplied input to the Cube server without sufficient sanitization, allowing command injection and arbitrary command execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Passing unsanitized user input to command execution interfaces is a classic injection vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should be strictly validated and escaped before being used in commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate commands may be constructed from user input, but only with strict validation.
key_indicators: Direct use of user input in command context

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies a vulnerable GitLab instance and crafts malicious requests targeting one or more vulnerabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation, internal resource access, denial-of-service, or remote command execution.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-6678 is exploited, attacker triggers pipelines as other users, potentially running arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation and potential code execution.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-8635 is exploited, attacker uses SSRF to access internal services or sensitive metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Internal data exposure or further lateral movement.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-8124 is exploited, attacker sends large glm_source parameter to exhaust resources and cause DoS.
If CVE-2024-8640 is exploited, attacker injects commands into Cube server, achieving arbitrary command execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and potential full compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Pipeline triggered by unexpected or unauthorized users
Dependency proxy requests to internal or non-standard URLs
API requests with abnormally large glm_source parameters
User input passed directly to command execution interfaces
file_indicators: Unusual pipeline logs showing user impersonation
Logs of dependency proxy fetching from internal IPs
API logs with large glm_source parameter values
Cube server logs with unexpected command patterns
network_indicators: Outbound requests from GitLab server to internal network addresses
High volume of API requests with large payloads
Unexpected command-and-control traffic if command injection is successful
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor pipeline trigger logs for user impersonation, inspect dependency proxy logs for requests to internal or non-standard URLs, set alerts for API requests with excessively large glm_source parameters, and audit command execution logs for unsanitized user input. Employ WAF rules to block suspicious payloads and implement strict input validation on all user-supplied data.
